question: What is a lie you told that accidentally made your life better?
story: I ran a fake tutoring club out of my high school library for two years, and the school gave me a leadership award for it. It started as a lie to get out of gym class. I told the front office I wanted to launch a peer tutoring group, and they handed me a room, a sign up sheet, and a free period. Small problem. I could not tutor anything. So every Tuesday, eleven kids showed up, and I told them to help each other while I sat at the front looking official with a clipboard. Nobody complained. Grades actually went up. Measurably. It turns out kids explain things to each other better than adults do. By senior year we had forty members and a waiting list. At graduation, the principal handed me a plaque for founding it. I have never worked so hard at doing absolutely nothing.
